Shun Ishiwaka Trio featuring Yusei Takahashi and Marty Holoubek with guest Tomoaki Baba clears RADAR admission on performance-specific grounds: Okegawa is the final published date of the quartet's first hall tour around Mabui, an all-Ishiwaka-composition project whose four players share Terumasa Hino-group lineage and whose instrumentation combines drums, piano/electric piano and electronics, bass, and tenor saxophone. events.factual_description: Okegawa Civic Hall presents Shun Ishiwaka Trio Hall Tour 2026+27 featuring Yusei Takahashi and Marty Holoubek with guest Tomoaki Baba on January 31, 2027. Doors are at 3:00 PM and the concert starts at 3:30 PM. The venue bills this as the group's first tour. Universal Music Japan lists Okegawa as the last published date of the six-city hall tour supporting Mabui. The album features Ishiwaka on drums, Takahashi on piano, electric piano, sampler and modular synthesizer, Holoubek on bass, and Baba on tenor saxophone; all eight compositions are by Ishiwaka. Universal Music Japan states that all four musicians are members of Terumasa Hino's group and describes the project as dynamic, robust interplay shaped by that shared lineage. The venue lists advance reserved seating at ¥5,000, same-day reserved seating at ¥5,500, and U25 tickets at ¥3,500.

en.why_it_matters: This is a strong snapshot of where the younger Japanese jazz thread is heading. Ishiwaka, Takahashi and Holoubek bring the new trio's first hall tour to its published closing date with Tomoaki Baba, turning Mabui's all-Ishiwaka book into a four-way conversation shaped by a shared Terumasa Hino lineage. The setup has real instrumental character—drums, acoustic and electric keys with electronics, bass and tenor sax—and the ALFIE connection in the trio's first record makes the project especially legible inside Listening Notes without making that connection the reason for admission.
en.trip_verdict: If a Kanto stay overlaps January 31, make room for the afternoon in Okegawa. The 3:30 PM start makes this a deliberate excursion beyond central Tokyo while still leaving the evening open for another plan.

es.why_it_matters: Es una fotografía muy buena de hacia dónde se mueve la vertiente joven del jazz japonés. Ishiwaka, Takahashi y Holoubek llevan la primera gira de salas del nuevo trío a su última fecha publicada con Tomoaki Baba, convirtiendo el repertorio íntegramente compuesto por Ishiwaka para Mabui en una conversación de cuatro músicos atravesada por una formación común junto a Terumasa Hino. La instrumentación tiene identidad propia —batería, piano y teclados eléctricos con electrónica, bajo y sax tenor— y el antecedente de ALFIE en el primer disco del trío conecta de manera natural con Listening Notes sin ser, por sí solo, la razón para admitir el concierto.
es.trip_verdict: Si una estancia en Kanto coincide con el 31 de enero, sí haría espacio para la tarde en Okegawa. El inicio a las 15:30 permite convertirlo en una salida deliberada fuera del centro de Tokio y todavía dejar libre la noche para otro plan.
